change.author: Julius Marminge

findings.title: card/dialog secret inputs render the saved redaction marker as the draft value
findings.body: In the `card` and `dialog` branches (lines 516-546) a secret field gets `SecretInput` with `value={readProviderConfigString(value, field.key)}` and no `configured`. `SecretInput` documents that `value` must be only the replacement draft. For a saved secret, the server sends the marker "••••••", so the card input shows the marker as its text with a "Not set" placeholder. The `dialog` branch uses `SecretInput` without `onCommit`, which renders a controlled `Input`. Typing there appends to the marker and saves "••••••abc" as the new secret, because the server only treats an exact marker match as "keep". The `settings` branch (line 415) does this correctly with `value=""` and `configured`. I found no caller that passes `variant="card"` or `variant="dialog"` (the callers I grepped all use `settings`), so this is latent. It will break when one is used. Either remove the unused secret handling from those branches or use the same `value=""` plus `configured` approach.

findings.title: Provider secret-field registry is a hand-maintained driver list
findings.body: The change is meant to make secrets "schema-declared", but `providerSecretFields` hard-codes the driver kinds (codex, claudeAgent, antigravity and six client definitions). A driver added later that marks a field with `secretSetting` and is not added here keeps that value as plaintext in settings.json. It is also sent unredacted to clients, with no error or test failing. Nothing links this list to the set of registered drivers. Consider deriving it from the provider client registry, or adding a test that every registered driver's settings schema is covered.

findings.title: Migration warning no longer says which secret failed to move
findings.body: The old warning logged `kind` and `field` for the source control host secret. The new `Effect.logWarning("failed to move a settings secret into the secret store")` logs nothing that identifies the secret. When several credentials across providers, hosts and quota sources are migrated, a failed move cannot be traced. Adding `secretName`, which is base64 of ids and not a secret value, would restore the context.

findings.title: "Preserves a configured secret on empty edits" does not exercise the `configured` guard
findings.body: The first test renders `configured value=""` and calls `edit("")`. `useCommitOnBlur` (apps/web/src/hooks/useCommitOnBlur.ts:32) already skips `onCommit` when `next === value`, and `"" === ""` here. So the test passes with or without the `if (configured && next === "") return;` check in SecretInput.tsx:32. That check can only fire when `configured` is true and `value` is non-empty, which the prop docs forbid and ProviderSettingsForm.tsx:422 never does. Either drop the guard, or test it with a case where it matters (for example `configured value="x"`). As written, the test name claims coverage it does not give.

contracts.action: Provider instance `config` secret fields (e.g. Antigravity apiKey) are now stored in the secret store, redacted for clients, and migrated from plaintext on load
contracts.equivalent_path: Provider environment secrets and source-control host secrets already went through the same store/redact/materialize/persist path in serverSettings.ts; this part folds them into one `mapSettingsSecrets` walker.
contracts.before_after: Before: apiKey stayed plaintext in settings.json and reached clients (client form hid it with a placeholder). After: moveInlineSettingsSecrets moves it on load (serverSettings.ts:690-717), persistSettingsSecrets writes and removes store entries (932-987), materializeSettingsSecrets rehydrates for getSettings/withSettingsSnapshot (869-904), and redactServerSettingsForClient blanks it (147-153).
contracts.visible_effect: Settings UI shows `Stored secret, enter a new value to replace` for a configured key. Providers read the real key through the materialized getSettings.
contracts.failure_mode: If a store read fails, getSettings fails for every secret type, which was already true for env/host/quota secrets. If the store write fails during load migration, the secret stays in the file and is retried on the next load. During updates, applySettingsSecretChanges rolls back on materialize or file-write failure.

contracts.action: SecretInput replaces password inputs in provider settings, env vars, GitHub token and usage-limit key
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous per-site `DraftInput`/`Input type="password"` with ad-hoc placeholders and `secretFieldInputProps`.
contracts.before_after: Before: each site set its own placeholder and the form suppressed empty commits for secrets. After: SecretInput sets the placeholder from `configured` and suppresses an empty commit when `configured`, with `value=""` as the draft in the settings variant.
contracts.visible_effect: Consistent placeholder text. A saved secret cannot be cleared by committing an empty field (same as before).
contracts.failure_mode: card/dialog variants of ProviderSettingsForm pass the saved marker as the draft value (see finding). No caller of those variants found.

contracts.action: Secret fields are marked by a `settingsSecret` key annotation (`secretSetting`) instead of `providerSettingsForm.secret`; `secretSettingsFields` and `isSecretSetting` read it for server persistence and client redaction
contracts.equivalent_path: The removed `secretSourceControlHostSettingsFields` in packages/source-control-core/src/client/definition.ts read `providerSettingsForm.secret` with the same `resolveAnnotationsKey(...) ?? resolveAnnotations(...)` lookup.
contracts.before_after: Before, only source control host settings honored the flag. Now providers (Antigravity `apiKey`) and usage-limit sources (`managementKey`) are marked as well. `secretSetting` is applied before `Schema.withDecodingDefault` in Antigravity and GitCafe. `withDecodingDefault` is `optional(toEncoded(self)).pipe(decodeTo(self, ...))`, which appends an encoding link to `self.ast`. The result therefore keeps `self`'s context, and the later `Schema.annotateKey` merges with `{...existing, ...new}`. So `settingsSecret` survives both orderings.
contracts.visible_effect: Secret fields are stored in the secret store and clients see only the redaction marker or a configured flag. The Antigravity description now says "Stored separately on the host."
contracts.failure_mode: `isSecretSetting` falls back to `resolveAnnotations` only when there are no key annotations. A schema-level `settingsSecret` combined with other key annotations would be missed, but nothing in this change does that. OpenCode `serverPassword` (packages/provider-opencode/src/settings.ts:45-51) still uses `control: "password"` without `secretSetting` and says it is stored in plain text, so it is left unmigrated.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 2.** Part 1 folds provider config, env, host and quota secrets into one `mapSettingsSecrets` walker. I traced the load/migrate, persist/rollback, materialize and redact paths against the old code and found them behaviourally equivalent, plus the new provider-config secrets. Findings are minor: the card/dialog variants of ProviderSettingsForm pass the redaction marker as the draft value (no current callers), the provider secret-field registry is a manual driver list, and the load-migration warning lost the field context. I read the code only and did not run the tests.

**Batch 2 of 2.** The contract and definition changes are coherent. `settingsSecret` survives `withDecodingDefault` in every ordering used. The old `secretSourceControlHostSettingsFields` and `providerSettingsForm.secret` have no remaining references. The only finding is in the SecretInput test: its "configured" case passes even without the guard it is named for.
